scoring_breakdown.font_name: 0.5 - All runs use Times New Roman
scoring_breakdown.bold: 0.5 - At least 90% of text-bearing runs are bold

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks both sub-goals from the instruction: font change to Times New Roman (0.5 pts) and bold formatting (0.5 pts) with partial credit scoring.
Getter retrieves the actual saved .docx file from the VM and parses all paragraph runs via python-docx, making it a file-state based check rather than a UI-based check.
Negative control resistance is good: the original document uses Georgia non-bold, so the initial state would score 0.0 for both checks.

Bold check uses 'r.bold is True' (strict identity) rather than truthiness, correctly distinguishing explicitly-set bold from style-inherited (None) bold. The 90% threshold adds tolerance for minor edge cases.
Font name check requires both 'font_name == Times New Roman' and 'all_same_font', verifying uniformity across the document.

Minor: 'expected_bold' key in the expected rules dict is never read by the metric function; the bold check is hardcoded rather than using expected['expected_bold']. This does not affect correctness for this task but reduces generalizability.

Minor: font names inherited from paragraph/document styles (where run.font.name is None) are excluded from the font_names list. After a Select All + font change via toolbar, LibreOffice typically writes the font explicitly to runs, so this is acceptable in practice but could miss style-inherited fonts if the agent used a style-based approach.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Use expected.get('expected_bold', True) in the metric to compare against the expected bold value rather than hardcoding the check for all_bold.

Consider also checking paragraph-level and style-level font settings (via paragraph.style or run.font.name falling back to paragraph style) to handle cases where the agent changed fonts via paragraph styles rather than direct run formatting.
